## QUESTION 1 
```{r}
## Creating my own per capita income from household  income variable 
# creating household size from given variables 

FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1 <- HH_DATA |>
  mutate(
    family_size = NADULTM + NADULTF + NCHILDM + NCHILDF + NTEENM + NTEENF + NELDERM + NELDERF,
    income_pc_constructed = INCOME / family_size) |>
  select(INCOME, family_size, income_pc_constructed, INCOMEPC)

# Check for missing values
summary(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1)

# Some Oultiers in Income and Per Capita so we need to remove them
#Remove negative values and zeros
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1 <- FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1 |>
  filter(income_pc_constructed > 0, INCOMEPC > 0)


# CHECKING SUMMARY AGAIN TO MATCH 
summary(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1)

# THERE IS DIFFERENCE BETWEEN INCOMEPC AND income_pc_constructed lets know this difference
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1 <- FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1 |>
  mutate(
    difference = income_pc_constructed - INCOMEPC,
    pct_diff = (difference / INCOMEPC) * 100)

summary(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1$difference)
summary(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1$pct_diff)

# So if we look into summary of it the median is around 0  for both cases means our correlation is strong and this difference is may be due to some small differences in household sizes and rounding of eorrors. 


## CORRELATION BETWEEEN THE CONSTRUCTED ADN ORIGINAL INCOMEPC 
# PLOT CORRELATION BETWEEN CONSTRUCTED AND GIVEN PER CAPITA INCOME
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = INCOMEPC, y = income_pc_constructed)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_smooth(se = TRUE, method = "lm", color = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Red dashed line = Perfect correlation", 
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = -0.5, color = "red", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = "Blue line = Actual relationship", 
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = -2, color = "darkblue", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation between Constructed and Given Per Capita Income (Ramesh Beniwal)",
    x = "Given Per Capita Income (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    y = "Constructed Per Capita Income (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    subtitle = "Check Median difference above = 0 | Correlation is very strong") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray40"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10))

# coefficient for correlation
FINAL_EXAM$correlation_q1 <- cor(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1$INCOMEPC,FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q1$income_pc_constructed)

print(paste("Correlation coefficient (Q1):", round(FINAL_EXAM$correlation_q1, 2)))
print(paste("Interpretation: Very strong positive correlation - constructed and given per capita income are highly similar"))
```

## QUESTION 2 
```{r}
# ASSUMPTION - Y GOES UP ~ C GOES UP 
# VALIDATION BY RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN COPC AND income_pc_constructed

# PART1
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 <- HH_DATA |>
  mutate(
    family_size = NADULTM + NADULTF + NCHILDM + NCHILDF + NTEENM + NTEENF + NELDERM + NELDERF,
    income_pc_constructed = INCOME / family_size
  ) |>
  select(income_pc_constructed, INCOMEPC, COPC) |>
  filter(income_pc_constructed > 0, INCOMEPC > 0, COPC > 0)

summary(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2)
```

```{r}

#BOXPLOT - Check outliers in COPC before filtering
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 |>
  ggplot(aes(y = COPC)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "orange", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot of Per Capita Consumption - Identifying Outliers (Ramesh Beniwal)",
    y = "Per Capita Consumption (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_blank())

```
```{r}
# BOXPLOT FOR CONSTRUCTED PER CAPITA INCOME
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 |>
  ggplot(aes(y = income_pc_constructed)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot of Constructed Per Capita Income - Identifying Outliers (Ramesh Beniwal)",
    y = "Constructed Per Capita Income (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_blank())
```


```{r}
# BOXPLOT FOR GIVEN PER CAPITA INCOME
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 |>
  ggplot(aes(y = INCOMEPC)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightgreen", color = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Boxplot of Given Per Capita Income - Identifying Outliers (Ramesh Beniwal)",
    y = "Given Per Capita Income (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_blank())
```


```{r}
# Remove outliers from COPC and other variables
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 <- FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 |>
  filter(COPC < 600000, income_pc_constructed < 900000, INCOMEPC < 900000)

summary(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2)
```

```{r}
# Both relationships on same graph
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = INCOMEPC, y = COPC, color = "Given Per Capita Income"), 
              se = TRUE, method = "lm", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(aes(x = income_pc_constructed, y = COPC, color = "Constructed Per Capita Income"), 
              se = TRUE, method = "lm", linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Income-Consumption Relationship: Validation of Assumption (Ramesh Beniwal)",
    x = "Per Capita Income (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    y = "Per Capita Consumption (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    color = "Income Measure [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    subtitle = "shows positive relationship- As income increases, consumption increases") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray40"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
# side by side
FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2_side<- FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2 |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(INCOMEPC, income_pc_constructed),
               names_to = "income_type",
               values_to = "income_value") |>
  mutate(income_type = case_when(
    income_type == "INCOMEPC" ~ "Given Per Capita Income",
    income_type == "income_pc_constructed" ~ "Constructed Per Capita Income"))

FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2_side|>
  ggplot(aes(x = income_value, y = COPC, color = income_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1.5) +
  geom_smooth(se = TRUE, method = "lm", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~income_type, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(
    title = "Income-Consumption Relationship by Income Type (Ramesh Beniwal)",
    x = "Per Capita Income (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    y = "Per Capita Consumption (Rupees) [Ramesh Beniwal]",
    color = "Income Measure [Ramesh Beniwal]") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#Cor calculation for both 
FINAL_EXAM$cor_given_income <- cor(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2$INCOMEPC, FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2$COPC)
FINAL_EXAM$cor_constructed_income <- cor(FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2$income_pc_constructed, FINAL_EXAM$HH_DATA_q2$COPC)
```

```{r}
# Results / Print
print(paste("Correlation (Given Per Capita Income vs Consumption):", round(FINAL_EXAM$cor_given_income, 2)))
print(paste("Correlation (Constructed Per Capita Income vs Consumption):", round(FINAL_EXAM$cor_constructed_income, 2)))
print("INTERPRETATION: ASSUMPTION VALIDATED - Both income measures show POSITIVE correlation with consumption")
print("As per capita income increases, per capita consumption also increases")
```

## INTERPRETATION

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Findings
**Correlation Coefficients:**
- **Given Per Capita Income vs Consumption:** 0.49
- **Constructed Per Capita Income vs Consumption:** 0.48

**Interpretation:**

Both per capita income measures ( manually and given ) show a **POSITIVE correlation** (approximately 0.48-0.49) with per capita consumption, which **VALIDATES the assumption** that as income increases, consumption also increases.

**Key Observations:**

1. **Positive Relationship:** The correlation of ~0.48 indicates a positive relationship between income and consumption.

2. **Both Measures Consistent:** The constructed per capita income and given per capita income show nearly identical correlations (0.49 vs 0.48), confirming our constructed income variable is valid.

3. **Assumption Validated:** The economic assumption that consumption increases with income is **CONFIRMED** as per Household Data we are using.

**Conclusion:**

The analysis provides evidence supporting the economic thinking and assumption of positive income-consumption relationship. Both graphs and correlation shows that their is positive relationships between them and positively related to each other.
:::
